title: Caracal: A GPU-Resident Sparse LU Solver with Lightweight Fine-Grained Scheduling
problem: Inefficiencies in task scheduling, memory management, and scalability in GPU-resident sparse LU factorization limit the performance of sparse solvers on GPU clusters.
motivation: Existing sparse LU solvers suffer from suboptimal task scheduling overhead, inefficient GPU memory utilization, and poor inter-GPU communication patterns. Achieving high computational throughput and scalability on multi-GPU systems requires addressing these bottlenecks.
method: Two-level scheduling approach: (1) coarse-grained blocks with sequential scheduling, (2) fine-grained blocks managed with lightweight static scheduler enabling multi-stream parallelism. Intelligent memory caching retains frequently accessed data. 1D block-cyclic matrix distribution optimizes NVLink inter-GPU communication.
key_novelty: Lightweight static fine-grained scheduler with intelligent memory caching and optimized 1D block-cyclic distribution for multi-GPU sparse LU, achieving practical scalability on modern GPUs.
contributions: Two-level hierarchical scheduling combining coarse-grained sequential and fine-grained lightweight scheduling
Intelligent GPU memory caching mechanism for frequently accessed data
1D block-cyclic matrix distribution optimizing NVLink communication
7x speedup over SuperLU_DIST, 94x over PanguLU, 16x over PasTiX
limitations: Results limited to 4 A100 GPUs; larger-scale evaluation needed. Full scalability analysis beyond 4 GPUs not presented. Comparison with recent GPU-native solvers limited.
